short_definition: Source-specific frequency, visibility, or attention trace.
visual_function: Places a change signal in a named source boundary.
typical_source_or_material: Google Books Ngram, recovered search frequency, aggregate visibility data.
claim_allowed: Selected forms become more or less visible in a named source.
claim_not_allowed: Total cultural importance, first historical use, all English usage.

short_definition: Documented occurrence or lexical evidence anchor.
visual_function: Separates evidence of occurrence from trend visibility.
typical_source_or_material: Dictionary pointers, public-domain scans, legal or lexical source anchors.
claim_allowed: A source documents a usage or sense at a particular point.
claim_not_allowed: The absolute first use in history or every community of use.
example_component_or_page: Hub evidence anchors; Privacy legal injury anchors; EvidenceArchive

short_definition: Declared policy for forms, spellings, compounds, phrases, and semantic families.
visual_function: Shows what has been grouped, separated, or kept adjacent.
typical_source_or_material: Curated forms, phrase sets, grammatical status, X + word and word + X patterns.
claim_allowed: The interface is reading these forms together under an explicit rule.
claim_not_allowed: The grouped forms are automatically identical meanings or dictionary senses.
example_component_or_page: DataDatumRoute; Artificial semantic attractor; Hub naming machine

short_definition: Examples, snippets, domains, and interpretive surroundings.
visual_function: Connects chart signals to local usage environments.
typical_source_or_material: Gutenberg snippets, Wikinews captures, source summaries, domain references.
claim_allowed: A usage environment supports a contextual interpretation.
claim_not_allowed: A snippet explains all historical meaning or all usage communities.
example_component_or_page: DataSocializedGeneration; Hub transfer model; Privacy semantic weather

short_definition: Explicit limits on what the visual evidence can claim.
visual_function: Turns uncertainty and non-claims into visible interface material.
typical_source_or_material: Caution notes, do-not-claim lists, missing evidence labels, source-boundary text.
claim_allowed: The reader can see where the claim stops.
claim_not_allowed: A limitation is hidden or treated as irrelevant footnote material.
example_component_or_page: Hub centrality rebuild; Data cross pressures; About page claim limits

short_definition: Attribution, source terms, and reuse conditions.
visual_function: Makes evidence provenance and publication constraints part of the display.
typical_source_or_material: Source ledgers, rights status, citation notes, public-domain/restricted labels.
claim_allowed: Evidence can be cited, inspected, or reused according to named conditions.
claim_not_allowed: The project owns all source material or may republish restricted text freely.
